claim: DIPPER is a deep and comprehensive IVD proteomic resource comprising 94 genome-wide profiles from 17 individuals.
source: We present DIPPER, a deep and comprehensive IVD proteomic resource comprising 94 genome-wide profiles from 17 individuals.
evidence: Stated directly in the abstract with specific numbers of profiles and individuals.

claim: Protein modules defining key directional trends spanning the lateral and anteroposterior axes were derived from high-resolution spatial proteomes of intact young cadaveric lumbar IVDs.
source: To begin with, protein modules defining key directional trends spanning the lateral and anteroposterior axes were derived from high-resolution spatial proteomes of intact young cadaveric lumbar IVDs.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract describing the methodology and findings.

claim: The protein modules revealed novel region-specific profiles of regulatory activities.
source: They revealed novel region-specific profiles of regulatory activities and displayed potential paths of deconstruction in the level- and location-matched aged cadaveric discs.
evidence: Stated as a finding from the analysis of protein modules.

claim: Machine learning methods predicted a 'hydration matrisome' that connects extracellular matrix with MRI intensity.
source: Machine learning methods predicted a 'hydration matrisome' that connects extracellular matrix with MRI intensity.
evidence: Explicitly stated as a finding using machine learning methods.

claim: The static proteome can be integrated with dynamic proteome (SILAC/degradome) and transcriptome data from multiple clinical samples.
source: Importantly, the static proteome used as point-references can be integrated with dynamic proteome (SILAC/degradome) and transcriptome data from multiple clinical samples, enhancing robustness and clinical relevance.
evidence: Stated as a key feature of the DIPPER resource.

claim: IVD degeneration is most common in the lumbar region.
source: IVD degeneration (IDD), most common in the lumbar region (Saleem et al., 2013; Teraguchi et al., 2014), is associated with a decline in function and a major cause of back pain, affecting up to 80% of the world's population at some point in life (Rubin, 2007), presenting significant socioeconomic burdens.
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: IVD degeneration affects up to 80% of the world's population at some point in life.
source: IVD degeneration (IDD), most common in the lumbar region (Saleem et al., 2013; Teraguchi et al., 2014), is associated with a decline in function and a major cause of back pain, affecting up to 80% of the world's population at some point in life (Rubin, 2007), presenting significant socioeconomic burdens.
evidence: Supported by citation to Rubin, 2007.

claim: Multiple interacting factors such as genetics, influenced by ageing, mechanical and other stress factors, contribute to the pathobiology, onset, severity, and progression of IDD.
source: Multiple interacting factors such as genetics, influenced by ageing, mechanical and other stress factors, contribute to the pathobiology, onset, severity, and progression of IDD (Munir et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Munir et al., 2018.

claim: IVDs are large, avascular, extracellular matrix (ECM)-rich structures comprising three compartments: nucleus pulposus (NP), annulus fibrosus (AF), and cartilaginous endplates.
source: IVDs are large, avascular, extracellular matrix (ECM)-rich structures comprising three compartments: a hydrated nucleus pulposus (NP) at the centre, surrounded by a tough annulus fibrosus (AF) at the periphery, and cartilaginous endplates of the adjoining vertebral bodies (Humzah and Soames, 1988).
evidence: Supported by citation to Humzah and Soames, 1988.

claim: The early adolescent NP is populated with vacuolated notochordal-like cells, which are gradually replaced by small chondrocyte-like cells.
source: The early adolescent NP is populated with vacuolated notochordal-like cells, which are gradually replaced by small chondrocyte-like cells (Risbud et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Risbud et al., 2015.

claim: Blood vessels terminate at the endplates, nourishing and oxygenating the NP via diffusion.
source: Blood vessels terminate at the endplates, nourishing and oxygenating the NP via diffusion, whose limited capacity mean that NP cells are constantly subject to hypoxic, metabolic, and mechanical stresses (Urban et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citation to Urban et al., 2004.

claim: With ageing and degeneration, there is an overall decline in cell 'health' and numbers.
source: With ageing and degeneration, there is an overall decline in cell 'health' and numbers (Rodriguez et al., 2011; Sakai et al., 2012), disrupting homeostasis of the disc proteome.
evidence: Supported by citations to Rodriguez et al., 2011 and Sakai et al., 2012.

claim: A hallmark of IDD is reduced hydration in the NP, diminishing the disc's capacity to dissipate mechanical loads.
source: Indeed, a hallmark of IDD is reduced hydration in the NP, diminishing the disc's capacity to dissipate mechanical loads.
evidence: Stated as a known characteristic of IDD.

claim: T-2 weighted MRI is the gold standard for assessing IDD.
source: Clinically, T-2 weighted MRI is the gold standard for assessing IDD, that uses disc hydration and structural features such as bulging or annular tears to measure severity (Pfirrmann et al., 2001; Schneiderman et al., 1987).
evidence: Supported by citations to Pfirrmann et al., 2001 and Schneiderman et al., 1987.

claim: The hydration and mechanical properties of the IVD are dictated by the ECM composition.
source: The hydration and mechanical properties of the IVD are dictated by the ECM composition, which is produced and maintained by the IVD cells.
evidence: Stated as a fundamental principle of IVD biology.

claim: Cells in the IVD compartments synthesise different compositions of ECM proteins to meet specific biomechanical needs.
source: To meet specific biomechanical needs, cells in the IVD compartments synthesise different compositions of ECM proteins.
evidence: Stated as a known biological principle.

claim: The ECM is defined as the 'matrisome'.
source: Defined as the 'matrisome' (Naba et al., 2012), the ECM houses the cells and facilitates their inter-communication by regulation of the availability and presentation of signalling molecules (Taha and Naba, 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Naba et al., 2012 and Taha and Naba, 2019.

claim: With ageing or degeneration, the NP becomes more fibrotic and less compliant.
source: With ageing or degeneration, the NP becomes more fibrotic and less compliant (Yee et al., 2016), ultimately affecting disc biomechanics (Newell et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Yee et al., 2016 and Newell et al., 2017.

claim: Changes in matrix stiffness can have a profound impact on cell-matrix interactions and downstream transcriptional regulation, signalling activity, and cell fate.
source: Changes in matrix stiffness can have a profound impact on cell-matrix interactions and downstream transcriptional regulation, signalling activity, and cell fate (Park et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Park et al., 2011.

claim: Many IDD genetic risk factors are variants in genes encoding matrisome proteins.
source: Notably, many of the associated IDD genetic risk factors, such as COL9A1 (Jim et al., 2005), ASPN (Song et al., 2008), and CHST3 (Song et al., 2013), are variants in genes encoding matrisome proteins, highlighting their importance for disc function.
evidence: Supported by citations to Jim et al., 2005, Song et al., 2008, and Song et al., 2013.

claim: Current knowledge of IVD biology is inferred from a limited number of transcriptomic studies on human and animal discs.
source: Current knowledge of IVD biology is inferred from a limited number of transcriptomic studies on human (Minogue et al., 2010; Riester et al., 2018; Rutges et al., 2010) and animal (Veras et al., 2020) discs.
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple transcriptomic studies.

claim: Cells in young healthy NP express markers including CD24, KRT8, KRT19, and T.
source: Studies showed that cells in young healthy NP express markers including CD24, KRT8, KRT19, and T (Fujita et al., 2005; Minogue et al., 2010; Rutges et al., 2010), whereas NP cells in aged or degenerated discs have different and variable molecular signatures (Chen et al., 2006; Rodrigues-Pinto et al., 2016), such as genes involved in TGFβ signalling (TGFA, INHA, INHBA, BMP2/6).
evidence: Supported by citations to Fujita et al., 2005, Minogue et al., 2010, and Rutges et al., 2010.

claim: The healthy AF expresses genes including collagens (COL1A1 and COL12A1).
source: The healthy AF expresses genes including collagens (COL1A1 and COL12A1) (van den Akker et al., 2017), growth factors (PDGFB, FGF9, VEGFC), and signalling molecules (NOTCH and WNT) (Riester et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to van den Akker et al., 2017 and Riester et al., 2018.

claim: Transcriptome-proteome discordance does not enable accurate predictions of protein levels from mRNA.
source: Although transcriptomic data provides valuable cellular information, it does not faithfully reflect the molecular composition. Cells represent only a small fraction of the disc volume, transcriptome-proteome discordance does not enable accurate predictions of protein levels from mRNA (Fortelny et al., 2017), and the disc matrisome accumulates and remodels over time.
evidence: Supported by citation to Fortelny et al., 2017.

claim: Proteomic studies on animal models of IDD have been reported, including murine, canine, and bovine models.
source: Proteomic studies on animal models of IDD, including murine (McCann et al., 2015), canine (Erwin et al., 2015), and bovine (Caldeira et al., 2017), have been reported.
evidence: Supported by citations to McCann et al., 2015, Erwin et al., 2015, and Caldeira et al., 2017.

claim: Human-animal differences in cellular phenotypes and mechanical loading physiologies mean that animal findings might not translate to the human scenario.
source: Nevertheless, human-animal differences in cellular phenotypes and mechanical loading physiologies mean that these findings might not translate to the human scenario.
evidence: Stated as a limitation of animal studies.

claim: Human proteomic studies have shown increases in fibrotic changes in aging and degeneration.
source: So far, human proteomic studies have compared IVDs with other cartilaginous tissues (Önnerfjord et al., 2012) and have shown increases in fibrotic changes in aging and degeneration (Yee et al., 2016), a role for inflammation in degenerated discs (Rajasekaran et al., 2020), the presence of haemoglobins and immunoglobulins in discs with spondylolisthesis and herniation (Maseda et al., 2016), and changes in proteins related to cell adhesion and migration in IDD (Sarath Babu et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Yee et al., 2016.

claim: The reported human disc proteomes were limited in the numbers of proteins identified and finer compartmentalisation within the IVD.
source: The reported human disc proteomes were limited in the numbers of proteins identified and finer compartmentalisation within the IVD, and disc levels along the lumbar spine have yet to be studied.
evidence: Stated as a limitation of previous studies.

claim: High-resolution static spatial proteomes were generated from multiple intact disc segments of young trauma-induced (16 M) and aged (57 M) cadaveric spines.
source: High-resolution static spatial proteomes were generated from multiple intact disc segments of young trauma-induced (16 M) and aged (57 M) cadaveric spines.
evidence: Stated as a methodological approach with specific ages.

claim: T1- and T2-weighted MRI (3T) showed the young discs (L3/4, L4/5, L5/S1) were non-degenerated, with a Schneiderman score of 1 from T2 images.
source: T1- and T2-weighted MRI (3T) showed the young discs (L3/4, L4/5, L5/S1) were non-degenerated, with a Schneiderman score of 1 from T2 images (Figure 1B).
evidence: Stated as an observation from MRI data, with reference to Figure 1B.

claim: The NP of young IVD were well hydrated (white) with no disc bulging, endplate changes, or observable inter-level variations.
source: The NP of young IVD were well hydrated (white) with no disc bulging, endplate changes, or observable inter-level variations (Figure 1B; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), consistent with healthy discs and were deemed fit to serve as a benchmarking point-reference.
evidence: Stated as an observation from MRI data, with reference to figures.

claim: All aged discs had irregular endplates, and annular tears were present adjacent to the lower endplate and extending towards the posterior region at L3/4 and L4/5.
source: All discs had irregular endplates, and annular tears were present (green arrowheads) adjacent to the lower endplate and extending towards the posterior region at L3/4 and L4/5 (Figure 1C).
evidence: Stated as an observation from high-resolution MRI, with reference to Figure 1C.

claim: The NP of aged discs exhibited regional variations in hydration in both sagittal and transverse images.
source: The NP exhibited regional variations in hydration in both sagittal and transverse images (Figure 1C).
evidence: Stated as an observation from MRI data, with reference to Figure 1C.

claim: Scoliosis was not detected in the two cadaveric individuals.
source: Scoliosis was not detected in these two individuals.
evidence: Stated as a clinical observation.

claim: A median of 654 proteins per profile were identified for the young samples and 829 proteins for the aged samples.
source: A median of 654 proteins per profile were identified for the young samples and 829 proteins for the aged samples, with a median of 742 proteins per profile for young and aged combined.
evidence: Stated as a quantitative result from the proteomic analysis.

claim: Of the 3100 proteins detected in total, 418 were matrisome proteins (40.7% of all known matrisome proteins) and 2682 non-matrisome proteins (~14% of genome-wide non-matrisome genes).
source: Of the 3100 proteins detected in total, 418 were matrisome proteins (40.7% of all known matrisome proteins) and 2682 non-matrisome proteins (~14% of genome-wide non-matrisome genes) (Figure 1E; Figure 1—figure supplement 1C), and 983 were common to all four major compartments, namely the OAF, IAF, NP/IAF, and NP (Figure 1E, upper panel).
evidence: Stated as a quantitative result with reference to figures.

claim: The aged OAF had the highest number of detected proteins with an average of 1156, followed by the young OAF with an average of 818.
source: The aged OAF had the highest number of detected proteins with an average of 1156, followed by the young OAF with an average of 818 (Figure 1F).
evidence: Stated as a quantitative result with reference to Figure 1F.

claim: The expression levels of core-matrisome were higher in young (median 30.74) than aged (median 29.72) discs.
source: Within the core-matrisome, the expression was higher (p=6.4 × 10−21) in young (median 30.74) than aged (median 29.72) discs (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C & D).
evidence: Stated as a statistical result with p-value and reference to figures.

claim: The levels of ECM proteins in each compartment of the disc declines with ageing.
source: That is, the levels of ECM proteins in each compartment of the disc declines with ageing and possibly changes in the relative composition, while the numbers of proteins detected per matrisome subcategory remain similar.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the data.

claim: With ageing, ECM synthesis is not sufficient to counterbalance degradation.
source: This agrees with the concept that with ageing, ECM synthesis is not sufficient to counterbalance degradation, as exemplified in a proteoglycan study (Silagi et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Silagi et al., 2018.

claim: Histone concentrations increased from the inner to the outer compartments of the disc.
source: Interestingly, histone concentrations, and thus cellularity, increased from the inner to the outer compartments of the disc, and showed a highly significant decrease in aged discs compared to young discs across all compartments (Figure 1J, Wilcoxon p=5.6 × 10−4 ; Figure 1—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: Stated as a result with statistical significance and reference to figures.

claim: Histone concentrations showed a highly significant decrease in aged discs compared to young discs across all compartments.
source: Interestingly, histone concentrations, and thus cellularity, increased from the inner to the outer compartments of the disc, and showed a highly significant decrease in aged discs compared to young discs across all compartments (Figure 1J, Wilcoxon p=5.6 × 10−4 ; Figure 1—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: Stated as a statistical result with p-value and reference to figures.

claim: GAPDH and ACTA2 amounts were significantly correlated with a Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) of 0.794.
source: GAPDH and ACTA2 amounts were significantly correlated with a Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) of 0.794 (p=9.3 × 10−9) (Figure 1—figure supplement 4C), and they were both significantly co-expressed with the detected histone subunits, with PCCs of 0.785 and 0.636, respectively (Figure 1K; Figure 1—figure supplement 4D).
evidence: Stated as a statistical result with correlation coefficient and p-value.

claim: The first two principal components (PCs) explained a combined 65.5% of the variance, with 39.9% and 25.6% for the first and second PCs, respectively.
source: The first two principal components (PCs) explained a combined 65.5% of the variance, with 39.9% and 25.6% for the first and second PCs, respectively (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: Stated as a result from PCA with reference to figures.

claim: PC1 was most informative to predict age, with a clear demarcation between the two age groups.
source: A support vector machine with polynomial kernel was trained to predict the boundaries: it showed PC1 to be most informative to predict age, with a clear demarcation between the two age groups (Figure 2A, vertical boundary), whereas PC2 distinguished disc sample localities, separating the inner compartments (NP, NP/IAF, and IAF) from the OAF (Figure 2A, horizontal boundary).
evidence: Stated as a result from machine learning analysis with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: PC2 distinguished disc sample localities, separating the inner compartments (NP, NP/IAF, and IAF) from the OAF.
source: A support vector machine with polynomial kernel was trained to predict the boundaries: it showed PC1 to be most informative to predict age, with a clear demarcation between the two age groups (Figure 2A, vertical boundary), whereas PC2 distinguished disc sample localities, separating the inner compartments (NP, NP/IAF, and IAF) from the OAF (Figure 2A, horizontal boundary).
evidence: Stated as a result from machine learning analysis with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: PC3 captured only 5.0% of the variance but distinguished disc level, separating the lowest level (L5/S1) from the rest of the lumbar discs (L3/4 and L4/5).
source: PC3 captured only 5.0% of the variance (Figure 2C & D), but it distinguished disc level, separating the lowest level (L5/S1) from the rest of the lumbar discs (L3/4 and L4/5) (Figure 2D, horizontal boundary).
evidence: Stated as a result from PCA with reference to figures.

claim: In the young discs, the dominant phenotype explaining the variances for all protein categories was disc compartment.
source: In the young discs, the dominant phenotype explaining the variances for all protein categories was disc compartment.
evidence: Stated as a result from ANOVA analysis.

claim: In aged discs, compartment is still relevant for non-matrisome proteins and collagen, but disc level and directions become influential for other protein categories.
source: In aged discs, compartment is still relevant for non-matrisome proteins and collagen, but disc level and directions become influential for other protein categories, which is consistent with variations in mechanical loading occurring in the discs with ageing and degeneration (Figure 2—figure supplement 1J).
evidence: Stated as a result from ANOVA analysis with reference to figure.

claim: In the combined (young and aged) disc samples, age was the dominant phenotype across major matrisome categories.
source: In the combined (young and aged) disc samples, age was the dominant phenotype across major matrisome categories, while compartment best explained the variance in non-matrisome, reflecting the expected changes in cellular (non-matrisome) and structural (matrisome) functions of the discs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: Stated as a result from ANOVA analysis with reference to figure.

claim: The detected proteome of the young discs accounts for 9.2% of the human proteome (or 1883 out of the 20,368 on UniProt).
source: The detected proteome of the young discs (Figure 3B) accounts for 9.2% of the human proteome (or 1883 out of the 20,368 on UniProt).
evidence: Stated as a quantitative result with reference to Figure 3B.

claim: A set of 671 DEPs (termed the 'variable set') was detected, containing both matrisome and non-matrisome proteins.
source: We detected a set of 671 DEPs (Supplementary file 2) (termed the 'variable set'), containing both matrisome and non-matrisome proteins (Figure 3D), and visualised in a heatmap (Figure 3—figure supplement 2), with identification of four modules (Y1-Y4).
evidence: Stated as a result from differential expression analysis with reference to figures.

claim: Module Y1 is functionally relevant to NP, containing previously reported NP and novel markers KRT19, CD109, KRT8 and CHRD.
source: Module Y1 is functionally relevant to NP, containing previously reported NP and novel markers KRT19, CD109, KRT8 and CHRD (Anderson et al., 2002), CHRDL2, SCUBE1 (Johnson et al., 2012), and CLEC3B.
evidence: Stated as a finding with citations to previous studies.

claim: Module Y2 was enriched in proteins for ECM organisation.
source: Module Y2 was enriched in proteins for ECM organisation (FDR q = 8.8 × 10−24); Y3 was enriched for proteins involved in smooth muscle contraction processes (FDR q = 8.96 × 10−19); and Y4 was enriched for proteins of the innate immune system (FDR q = 2.93 × 10−20).
evidence: Stated as a result from enrichment analysis with FDR values.

claim: Module Y3 was enriched for proteins involved in smooth muscle contraction processes.
source: Module Y2 was enriched in proteins for ECM organisation (FDR q = 8.8 × 10−24); Y3 was enriched for proteins involved in smooth muscle contraction processes (FDR q = 8.96 × 10−19); and Y4 was enriched for proteins of the innate immune system (FDR q = 2.93 × 10−20).
evidence: Stated as a result from enrichment analysis with FDR values.

claim: Module Y4 was enriched for proteins of the innate immune system.
source: Module Y2 was enriched in proteins for ECM organisation (FDR q = 8.8 × 10−24); Y3 was enriched for proteins involved in smooth muscle contraction processes (FDR q = 8.96 × 10−19); and Y4 was enriched for proteins of the innate immune system (FDR q = 2.93 × 10−20).
evidence: Stated as a result from enrichment analysis with FDR values.

claim: The inner disc regions were enriched in collagens (COL3A1, COL5A1, COL5A2, and COL11A2), matrillin (MATN3), and proteins associated with ECM synthesis (PCOLCE) and matrix remodelling (MXRA5).
source: Notably, OAF and inner disc contained different types of ECM proteins. The inner disc regions were enriched in collagens (COL3A1, COL5A1, COL5A2, and COL11A2), matrillin (MATN3), and proteins associated with ECM synthesis (PCOLCE) and matrix remodelling (MXRA5).
evidence: Stated as a result from differential expression analysis.

claim: The OAF is enriched with various collagens (COL1A1, COL6A1/2/3, COL12A1 and COL14A1), basement membrane (BM) proteins (LAMA4, LAMB2 and LAMC1), small leucine-rich proteoglycans (SLRP) (BGN, DCN, FMOD, OGN, PRELP), and BM-anchoring protein (PRELP).
source: The OAF is enriched with various collagens (COL1A1, COL6A1/2/3, COL12A1 and COL14A1), basement membrane (BM) proteins (LAMA4, LAMB2 and LAMC1), small leucine-rich proteoglycans (SLRP) (BGN, DCN, FMOD, OGN, PRELP), and BM-anchoring protein (PRELP) (Figure 3I,J).
evidence: Stated as a result from differential expression analysis with reference to figures.

claim: Tenomodulin (TNMD) was exclusively expressed in 9 of the 12 young OAF profiles, and not in any other compartments.
source: Tenomodulin (TNMD) was exclusively expressed in 9 of the 12 young OAF profiles, and not in any other compartments (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Stated as a result from the proteomic data.

claim: The constant set represents the baseline proteome among structures within the young disc.
source: We set a cutoff for a detection in >1/2 of the profiles to prioritise a set of 245 proteins, hereby referred to as the 'constant set' (Figure 3C).
evidence: Stated as a methodological approach with reference to Figure 3C.

claim: Amongst the proteins in the constant set that were detected in all 33 young profiles were known protein markers defining a young NP or disc, including COL2A1, ACAN, and A2M.
source: Amongst the proteins in the constant set that were detected in all 33 young profiles were known protein markers defining a young NP or disc, including COL2A1, ACAN, and A2M (Risbud et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated as a result with citation to Risbud et al., 2015.

claim: In the aged disc, 99 proteins were expressed higher in the OAF, similar to young discs.
source: Detection of DEPs between the OAF and the inner disc (Figure 4B), showed that 100 proteins were expressed higher in the OAF, similar to young discs (Figure 3C).
evidence: Stated as a result from differential expression analysis with reference to figures.

claim: In the inner regions of aged discs, only nine proteins were significantly expressed higher, in marked contrast to the situation in young discs.
source: However, in the inner regions, only nine proteins were significantly expressed higher, in marked contrast to the situation in young discs.
evidence: Stated as a result from differential expression analysis.

claim: The typical NP markers (KRT8/19, CD109, CHRD, CHRDL2) were not detectable as DEPs in the aged disc.
source: The typical NP markers (KRT8/19, CD109, CHRD, CHRDL2) were not detectable as DEPs in the aged disc; but CHI3L2, A2M and SERPING1 (Figure 4B), which have known roles in tissue fibrosis and wound healing (Lee et al., 2011; Naveau et al., 1994; Wang et al., 2019a), were detected uniquely in the aged discs.
evidence: Stated as a result from differential expression analysis with citations.

claim: The aged OAF retained 55% of the proteins of a young OAF.
source: A comparative analysis of the protein profiles indicated that the aged OAF retained 55% of the proteins of a young OAF.
evidence: Stated as a result from comparative analysis.

claim: 45 proteins enriched in the aged OAF could be classified under 'responses to stress'.
source: From a cellular perspective, 45 proteins enriched in the aged OAF could be classified under 'responses to stress' (FDR q = 1.86 × 10−7; contributed by CAT, PRDX6, HSP90AB1, EEF1A1, TUBB4B, P4HB, PRDX1, HSPA5, CRYAB, HIST1H1C), suggesting OAF ECM and cells are responding to a changing environment such as mechanical loading and other stress factors.
evidence: Stated as a result from enrichment analysis with FDR value.

claim: The protein composition of the inner disc compartments becomes more similar to the OAF with ageing, with the greatest changes in the inner regions.
source: These progressive changes of the protein profiles and DEPs between inner and outer compartments suggest the protein composition of the inner disc compartments becomes more similar to the OAF with ageing, with the greatest changes in the inner regions.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the data.

claim: 169 DEPs were identified between all 33 young samples and all 33 aged samples, with 104 expressed higher in the young and 65 expressed higher in the aged discs.
source: First, we compared all 33 young samples with all 33 aged samples, which identified 169 DEPs with 104 expressed higher in the young and 65 expressed higher in the aged discs (Figure 5A).
evidence: Stated as a result from differential expression analysis with reference to Figure 5A.

claim: The most important biological property for a young disc is structural integrity, which is lost in aged discs.
source: A simple gene ontology (GO) term analysis showed that the most important biological property for a young disc is structural integrity, which is lost in aged discs (Figure 5B; Supplementary file 5).
evidence: Stated as a result from GO term analysis with reference to figures.

claim: 75% (78/104) of the downregulated DEPs were attributed to the inner regions, and only 17% (18/104) were attributed to the OAF.
source: Seventy-five percent (78/104) of the downregulated DEPs (Figure 5F) were attributed to the inner regions, and only 17% (18/104) were attributed to the OAF (Figure 5F).
evidence: Stated as a quantitative result with reference to Figure 5F.

claim: 65% (42/65) of the upregulated DEPs were solely contributed by inner disc regions, and only 18.4% (12/65) by the OAF.
source: Similarly, 65% (42/65) of the upregulated DEPs were solely contributed by inner disc regions, and only 18.4% (12/65) by the OAF.
evidence: Stated as a quantitative result.

claim: Inhibitors of WNT (DKK3 and FRZB), and antagonists of BMP/TGFβ (CD109, CHRDL2, DCN FMOD, INHBA and THBS1) signalling were decreased or absent in the aged inner region.
source: Inhibitors of WNT (DKK3 and FRZB), and antagonists of BMP/TGFβ (CD109, CHRDL2, DCN FMOD, INHBA and THBS1) signalling were decreased or absent in the aged inner region (Figure 5F,G), consistent with the reported upregulation of these pathways in IDD (Hiyama et al., 2010) and its closely related condition osteoarthritis (Leijten et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated as a result with citations to previous studies.

claim: Targets of hedgehog signalling (HHIPL2 and SCUBE1) were reduced in aged discs.
source: Targets of hedgehog signalling (HHIPL2 and SCUBE1) were also reduced (Figure 5F), consistent with SHH's key roles in IVD development and maintenance (Rajesh and Dahia, 2018).
evidence: Stated as a result with citation to Rajesh and Dahia, 2018.

claim: Module 6 (M6) is enriched for proteins involved in the complement pathway and angiogenesis.
source: A striking feature is module 6 (M6), which is enriched for proteins involved in the complement pathway (GSEA Hallmark FDR q = 4.9 × 10−14) and angiogenesis (q = 2.3 × 10−3).
evidence: Stated as a result from enrichment analysis with FDR values.

claim: M6 contains proteins that are all highly expressed in the inner regions of the aged disc, suggesting the presence of blood.
source: This module contains proteins that are all highly expressed in the inner regions of the aged disc, suggesting the presence of blood.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the data.

claim: M6 also contains the macrophage marker CD14, which supports the notion of blood presence.
source: M6 also contains the macrophage marker CD14, which supports this notion.
evidence: Stated as supporting evidence for blood presence.

claim: PC1 of the transcriptome captured age/state variations and PC2 captured the compartment (AF or NP) differences.
source: PCA of the transcriptome profiles showed that PC1 captured age/state variations (Figure 6A) and PC2 captured the compartment (AF or NP) differences, with a high degree of similarity to the proteomic PCA that explained 65.0% of all data variance (Figure 2A).
evidence: Stated as a result from PCA with reference to figures.

claim: 88 DEGs were detected between young AF and young NP samples, in which 39 were more abundant in young NP and 49 were more abundant in young AF.
source: We detected 88 DEGs (Materials and methods) between young AF and young NP samples (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E),in which 39 were more abundant in young NP (including known NP markers CD24, KRT19) and 49 were more abundant in young AF, including the AF markers, COL1A1, and THBS1.
evidence: Stated as a result from differential expression analysis with reference to figure.

claim: In the AGD samples, 11 genes differed between AF and NP.
source: In the AGD samples, 11 genes differed between AF and NP (Figure 6—figure supplement 1F), comparable to the proteome profiles (Figure 4C).
evidence: Stated as a result from differential expression analysis with reference to figures.

claim: Between the YND and AGD AF, there were 45 DEGs.
source: Between the YND and AGD AF, there were 45 DEGs, with COL1A1 and MMP1 more abundant in YND and COL10A1, WNT signalling (WIF1, WNT16), inflammatory (TNFAIP6, CXCL14, IL11), and fibrosis-associated (FN1, CXCL14) genes more abundant in AGD (Figure 6—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: Stated as a result from differential expression analysis with reference to figure.

claim: The greatest difference was between YND and AGD NP, with 216 DEGs.
source: The greatest difference was between YND and AGD NP, with 216 DEGs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1H), with a marked loss of NP markers (KRT19, CD24), and gain of AF (THBS1, DCN), proteolytic (ADAMTS5), and EMT (COL1A1, COL3A1, PDPN, NT5E, LTBP1) markers with age.
evidence: Stated as a result from differential expression analysis with reference to figure.

claim: The number of proteins newly synthesised in the AGD samples was about half that in the YND samples.
source: The number of proteins newly synthesised in the AGD samples was about half that in the YND samples (Figure 7C).
evidence: Stated as a result from SILAC analysis with reference to Figure 7C.

claim: Of the 68 high abundant non-matrisome proteins in the YND NP compartment that were not present in the AGD NP, 28 are ribosomal proteins.
source: Of the 68 high abundant non-matrisome proteins in the YND NP compartment that were not present in the AGD NP, 28 are ribosomal proteins (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C), suggesting reduced translational activities.
evidence: Stated as a result from SILAC analysis with reference to figure.

claim: TAILS identified 123 and 84 cleaved proteins in the AF and NP disc samples, respectively.
source: Here, TAILS identified 123 and 84 cleaved proteins in the AF and NP disc samples, respectively.
evidence: Stated as a result from degradome analysis.

claim: The two YND samples (136 and 141) tend to cluster together in both AF and NP.
source: Performing hierarchical clustering on the data we found that the two YND samples (136 and 141; Table 1) tend to cluster together in both AF and NP (Figure 7G,H; Figure 7—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: Stated as a result from clustering analysis with reference to figures.

claim: The trauma sample AGD143 (53 year male) tends to cluster with other clinically diagnosed AGD samples, in both AF and NP.
source: Interestingly, the trauma sample AGD143 (53 year male), who has no known IDD diagnosis, tend to cluster with other clinically diagnosed AGD samples, in both AF and NP.
evidence: Stated as a result from clustering analysis.

claim: A LASSO regression model trained on the aged MRIs using the hydration matrisome predicted the intensity of the MRIs of the young discs with a PCC of 0.689.
source: To test this, we trained a LASSO regression model (Tibshirani, 1996) of the aged MRIs using the hydration matrisome (85 proteins), and applied the model to predict the intensity of the MRIs of the young discs, based on the young proteome of the same 85 proteins. Remarkably, we obtained a PCC of 0.689 (p=8.9 × 10−6; Spearman = 0.776) between the actual and predicted MRI (Figure 8—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Stated as a result from machine learning analysis with statistical values.

claim: The predicted MRI intensities of the young disc exhibited a smooth monotonic decrease from the NP towards IAF, then dropped suddenly towards the OAF.
source: The predicted MRI intensities of the young disc exhibited a smooth monotonic decrease from the NP towards IAF, then dropped suddenly towards the OAF (Figure 8F, right panel), with an ROC AUC (receiver operating characteristics, area under the curve) of 0.996 between IAF and OAF (Figure 8—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: Stated as a result from the LASSO model with reference to figures.
